rationale: Source investigation answers the remaining discriminator as a bounded delay rather than an unbounded stall, so the Candidate is explained by an existing mechanism instead of escalated. The gap itself is real and now recorded in the map: a higher-ballot AcceptReply is dropped at the equality gate (epaxos/epaxos.go:1024-1026) so handleAcceptReply never counts a nack or calls makeBallot/bcastPrepare. But non-completion at a ballot is not final for the instance. Every replica's executeCommands loop re-examines each row from ExecedUpTo+1 and, when a head instance stays non-executable for COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD, enqueues instancesToRecover for that instance (epaxos/epaxos.go:385-435); the local loop then runs startRecoveryForInstance, which rebuilds the instance bookkeeping and calls makeBallot then bcastPrepare (epaxos/epaxos.go:1127-1169). makeBallot chooses the recovering replica's own ballot slot, and for a replica that is not the row owner it uses r.Id + N, while an IsLeader additionally raises past maxRecvBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451), so a recovery attempt at an equal-or-higher ballot is available without the Accept-path escalation. Acceptors then adopt that prepare ballot (handlePrepare, epaxos/epaxos.go:1183-1187) and handlePrepareReply rebuilds the instance and re-enters Accept or phase 1 (epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1314). So the missing Accept-path nack costs at most the timer interval and a recovery round, not permanent stalling. I keep visible that this is a liveness/latency argument, not a proof of bounded latency, and that IsLeader gating and the non-leader ballot range bound how much a single recovery can raise the ballot.

feedback.answered: The dropped higher-ballot AcceptReply does not permanently stall the instance: the Accept path's missing escalation is replaced in practice by the executeCommands recovery timer, which enqueues a recovery for a non-advancing head instance after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD, and startRecoveryForInstance re-enters the ballot/Prapareo protocol at an equal-or-higher ballot (r.Id, r.Id+N, or above maxRecvBallot for a leader). The gap therefore costs a timer interval and a recovery round rather than losing progress, and the behavior now records both the real equality gate and the gap as an unknown.
remaining: Whether the delay can be extended by repeated failed recoveries when an acceptor holds a ballot higher than any a non-leader recoverer can produce (ballot range bounded by r.Id+N), which is a latency question rather than a permanent stall.
Grounding an explicit progress duty for the Accept path instead of relying on the recovery timer as an incidental protection.
A1 fast-path qualification and A2 ballot/authority transitions still have no executed check; membership (A4) and durability/restart (A6) remain unread.
feedback.rationale: Resolves the Candidate as bounded by an existing, sourced retry mechanism and keeps the residual latency/ballot-range and duty-grounding questions explicit.

question.question: When a coordinator's Accept replies report a higher ballot than lb.lastTriedBallot, does the coordinator ever escalate (count a nack, raise its ballot, issue Prepare), or are those replies dropped so the instance stalls until the recovery timer?
question.importance: Progress of the slow Accept path. Resolved: the Accept-path escalation is genuinely absent, but the instance is retried by the executeCommands recovery timer, so the effect is a delay rather than a permanent stall.
participants: coordinator in ACCEPTED status for the instance
acceptor replying with a higher instance ballot
any replica's executeCommands loop and recovery path
contexts: slow path after the fast quorum disagreed, so the coordinator broadcast Accept
concurrent recovery of the same instance at a higher ballot, bounded by COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD recovery retries
event_paths: handleAcceptReply equality gate (epaxos/epaxos.go:1024-1026) and unreachable greater-than block (epaxos/epaxos.go:1028-1035)
executeCommands COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD -> instancesToRecover -> startRecoveryForInstance -> makeBallot -> bcastPrepare (epaxos/epaxos.go:385-451, 1127-1169)
handlePrepare adopts the higher ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1183-1187); handlePrepareReply re-enters Accept or phase 1 (epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1314)

supporting_behavior_ids.B-EXEC: supplies the timer that re-enqueues the non-advancing instance for recovery, which is the mechanism that replaces the missing Accept-path escalation
supporting_behavior_ids.B-RECOVERY-START: rebuilds bookkeeping and issues the higher-ballot Prepare
supporting_behavior_ids.B-PREPARE-REPLY-LEADER: re-enters Accept or phase 1 and therefore can complete the instance
supporting_behavior_ids.B-PREACCEPT-REPLY-LEADER: shows the escalation that the Accept path lacks, and bounds the claim to progress rather than safety

counterevidence: The escalation block is still structurally unreachable, so the protection is not the handler's own nack logic but the independent recovery timer.

makeBallot does not always raise the ballot: for the row owner it reuses r.Id, and for a non-leader non-owner it is fixed at r.Id+N, so a recovery can fail against a higher stored ballot and only a later recovery by another replica or a leader can advance it.
unknowns: Whether repeated failed recoveries can extend the delay beyond one timer interval when a stored ballot exceeds any a non-leader recoverer can produce.
question.trigger_rationale: The specific suspicion (an instance that cannot complete because its coordinator never escalates) is answered by the sourced recovery retry, so it needs no execution; the residual latency and duty-grounding questions are retained.
